record.original_question: Let sum_{n=0}^{infinity} a_n be a conditionally divergent series of real numbers, and let S = {L in R : L = sum_{n=0}^{infinity} a_{sigma(n)} for some lambda-permutation sigma}. A lambda-permutation is, when applied to the index of a series, convergence-preserving and "fixing" at least one divergent series. Can S ever be something between empty set and R?

evidence.quote: In 2006, another mathematician Daniel Velleman raised an open problem related to λ-permutation: for a conditionally divergent series P∞ n=0 an, n ∈ N, an ∈ R, let S = {L ∈ R: L = P∞ n=0 aσ(n) for some λ-permutation σ}, can S ever be something between ∅ and R?
This type of permutation, when applied to the index of terms of series, is defined to be both convergence-preserving and "fixing" at least one divergent series

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n$ be a series of real numbers (indexed by $\mathbb{N}=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$). The series is called conditionally divergent if it diverges but can be rearranged into a convergent series, i.e., there exists a bijection $\tau:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_{\tau(n)}$ converges in $\mathbb{R}$.

A bijection $\sigma:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ is called a $\lambda$-permutation if it satisfies both of the following:
(i) (Convergence-preserving) For every series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} b_n$ of real numbers that converges in $\mathbb{R}$, the rearranged series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} b_{\sigma(n)}$ also converges (to the same sum).
(ii) (Fixes at least one divergent series) There exists at least one divergent series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} c_n$ of real numbers such that $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} c_{\sigma(n)}$ converges in $\mathbb{R}$.

Given a conditionally divergent series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n$, define
$$S \;=\; \Bigl\{\, L \in \mathbb{R} \;:\; L = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_{\sigma(n)} \text{ for some } \lambda\text{-permutation } \sigma \,\Bigr\}.$$

Question. Does there exist a conditionally divergent series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n$ for which the associated set $S$ is neither empty nor all of $\mathbb{R}$? Equivalently, must $S$ always be either $\emptyset$ or $\mathbb{R}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by Daniel Velleman in 2006, appears to remain open in general. Recent work (2025) addresses an analogous question for the subset of $S$ arising from "type R" $\lambda$-permutations, showing that this restricted subset is always empty, a singleton, or all of $\mathbb{R}$, and gives sufficient conditions for each case. This constitutes partial progress on a restricted variant rather than a full resolution of Velleman's original problem.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is referred to as Velleman's open problem and is addressed only for a restricted ('type R') subclass of λ-permutations.
